newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: LETTER ASKS PARISHONERS TO REJECT DIVISIVENESS RACISM

A letter signed by the heads of 11 of Australia's major Christian churches, challenging sentiments associated with Pauline Hanson, is being seen as a direct attack on several of the Independent MPs policies.
They've written to parishoners asking them to reject voices that encourage racism and divisiveness.
The letter asks parishoners to stand with Australia's indigenous people, whom it says are beyond doubt the country's most disadvantaged group.
It calls on Christians to cherish ethnic diversity, unmask falsehood parading as the truth, and resist the suggestion that any particular migrant group is to blame for the country's woes. - - - -
REITH CALL TO LIMIT WAGE RISES CRITICISED
A senior industrial relations researcher says it's hypocritical for Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith to criticise wage rises, set under his own regime, and which increase productivity.
Mr Reith says the four-point-eight per cent average increase in federal enterprise agreements threatens low inflation.
But John Buchanan of the Centre for Industrial Relations Research says Mr Reith's Workplace Relations Act calls on employers and employees to strike their own enterprise agreements.
Mr Buchanan says Mr Reith is telling the workplace to take responsibility for its wages and conditions, but wants to hammer it when it's makes decisions he doesn't like.
RAIL LINKS VYING FOR FEDERATION FUND DOLLARS
Competition is intensifying for a share of the new Federation Fund, announced in the federal budget.
The Northern Territory is hoping to secure funding for the Alice Springs to Darwin rail link.

But at tomorrow's National Transport Ministers conference, a group from the south-eastern states will table another project: a rail line to pass through primary production areas in three states to Mt Isa, and onto Darwin via Katherine.
In Cairns this morning, Territory Railway Minister Barry Coulter is expected to meet with Federal Transport Minister, John Sharp, to discuss the Alice to Darwin rail link.
STOLEN GENERATION REFERENCE GROUP TO MEET IN DARWIN
The Northern Territory's Stolen Generation Reference Group will meet today in Darwin, to consider the recommendations of a Human Rights Commission report.
The Commission looked at the past practice of forcibly separating Aboriginal families and has finalised its report, but the Federal government hasn't officially released it.
It's made more than 40 wide-ranging recommendations.
The report is expected to be a central focus of the national Aboriginal Reconciliation Convention in Melbourne next week.
15-year-old SHOT DEAD AT SUNSHINE
In Victoria, a 15-year-old teenage boy has been fatally shot while walking along a road at Sunshine, west of Melbourne, early this morning.
Homicide detectives are investigating the shooting, which was the result of a domestic incident.
At first, police thought the boy died in a drive-by shooting.
The boy was walking along Fairban Road about half-past-12, when he was shot by a driver at the intersection with Warmington Road.
Homicide detectives are questioning the man they believe is responsible.
MOBILE POLICE STATION SET UP AT KIDNAP SITE IN SYDNEY
Police have set up a mannequin today at the spot where Sydney kidnap victim Kerry Whelan was last seen, in the hope it may trigger the memory of witnesses to the crime.
There'll also be a mobile police station in place at the driveway of the Park Royal Hotel, at Phillip Street, in Parramatta in Sydney's west.
Mrs Whelan was abducted from a Parramatta carpark two weeks ago. Police hold grave fears for her safety.
AUSSIES DOING WELL IN DUSSELDORF
In tennis, the Australian team's upset win over the Americans in the World Team Cup in Germany, could be hold it in good stead when the two teams meet in the Davis Cup in September.
Australia will play the U-S in the sem-final of the Davis Cup in Washington.
Today the Aussies defeated the Czech Republic in Dusseldorf, three matches to nil, after upsetting the Americans, two matches to one, in the first round.
Mark Woodforde says beating the American side, which included Pete Sampras, Michael Chang and a formidable doubles team, was a good effort.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
